Salmon spawn in freshwater rivers to which they return after maturing at sea. Different species and populations use distinct rivers and tributaries, but all rely on rivers for spawning rather than lakes or oceans. For example, Pacific salmon such as chinook and sockeye spawn in large rivers like the Columbia and Snake or their tributaries [d3,d9], while coho return to natal river systems like the Coos and Coquille in Oregon [d5]. Atlantic salmon similarly return to rivers in which they were born, including specific rivers in Maine and Irish rivers [d6,d7]. Sockeye salmon also swim up rivers like the Chitina and Copper in Alaska to reach spawning grounds [d8]. Across regions and species, salmon consistently spawn in rivers rather than other water bodies [d1,d2,d4].
